# Multi-token prediction on a mini-PC — the measured decode recipe

One llama.cpp flag turns on the multi-token-prediction head already shipped
inside the Qwen3.8-27B GGUF everyone downloaded: paired measurements put
decode speed up +33% to +39% on the two founding 24 GB NVIDIA cards, and the
living community table spans +33% to +107% across ten rigs on both GPU
vendors, with the largest relative wins on bandwidth-poor mini-PC parts. No
new files, no conversion, no custom build. These notes restate the recipe, the
two tuning knobs, what breaks, and our own Strix Halo bench numbers.

## Canonical links

- This repo: https://github.com/simongonzalezdc/resonant-mtp-recipe
- Canonical community repo: https://github.com/sudoingX/qwen38-mtp (Apache-2.0) — the recipe, the founding paired A/B, the living table
- Bench companion: https://github.com/KyaniteLabs/qwen38-27b-strix-halo (MIT) — our Strix Halo numbers

## Key facts

- License: MIT
- Evidence labels preserved: PAIRED (the founding method, the only headline
  class), COMMUNITY (per-rig rows, absolutes not cross-comparable), SCREEN
  (shape, never ranking)
- Nothing here re-measures or re-brands anything

Relationship: community gift by Kyanite Labs for ResonantOS — canonical
source: https://github.com/sudoingX/qwen38-mtp; this adaptation is
non-canonical; where a number here ever disagrees with its source, the source
wins — flag an issue here or there.
